findings.title: claimTurn's 180 s lease predicate can be deleted with the entire agent-turn suite still green
findings.reason: Mutation t-m4 deleted the lease predicate from claimTurn's WHERE clause — the "claimed_at IS NULL OR claimed_at < NOW() - (leaseSeconds * INTERVAL '1 second')" arm — leaving only "status IN ('accepted','running')". The covering test, "worker claim race: two dispatches of one turn produce one completed turn and one proposal set" (src/lib/agents/operator/__tests__/turn-worker.integration.test.ts:319), still PASSED. A confirming run of the whole agent-turn test set under the same mutant — turn-worker.integration.test.ts + worker/jobs/agent-turn/__tests__ + turns.test.ts — reported 23 passed, 0 failed. The behavioural replacement: the concurrent section of that test (turn-worker.integration.test.ts:500-517) should assert that exactly one attempt reached the model and was billed (expect(runLlmTask).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) and one recordApiCost / api_costs row for the racy turn), and a direct claimTurn case should prove a second claim inside the lease returns null while one after lease expiry succeeds.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not an equivalent mutation. Deleting the lease predicate lets a second dispatch claim a turn whose 180 s lease is live (AGENT_TURN_LEASE_SECONDS, worker/jobs/agent-turn/constants.ts), so two attempts each run step 3, each build a snapshot and each make their own cost-guarded owner_operator model call. The intake's own risk_reasons names this consequence verbatim: "a new BullMQ worker (AgentTurnWorker) makes a cost-guarded LLM call ... a defect can double-bill or strand turns". Not an unexecuted branch either: the test's third section runs two handleAgentTurn calls under Promise.all on one freshly created turn, so both reach claimTurn inside the same lease window, and claimTurn is the first statement either executes after the flag gate. It survives because the assertions describe only the END STATE — one completed turn, one agent_proposals row, outbox completed — and completeTurnFenced's attempt_token fence delivers that end state on its own, independently of the lease. The lease predicate and the completion fence are two separate guards: the fence stops a stale attempt from WRITING, only the lease stops a second attempt from SPENDING. The suite asserts the first and never the second. Independently corroborated without spending a further run: "rg AGENT_TURN_LEASE_SECONDS|leaseSeconds|LEASE" across src/lib/agents/operator/__tests__ and worker/jobs/agent-turn/__tests__ returns no hit, the only two claimed_at writes in the suite (turn-worker.integration.test.ts:549, :585) drive loadPredecessor's age rather than the claim, and the claim-race test makes no runLlmTask or recordApiCost call-count assertion at all. Mutation t-m2, which removed completeTurnFenced's attempt_token fence, was KILLED — so the pair is asymmetric: the written-state half of the protocol is asserted and the spend half is not.

findings.title: The validator's allowedOperations gate is reached by no test

Both validator fixtures close that set — render.test.ts:31-35 lists set_tone, set_avoid_facts, read_pending_work; model-call.test.ts:57-60 lists set_tone, read_pending_work — and no test anywhere proposes set_products_services or set_highlight_facts through validateModelOutput (rg over src/lib/agents/operator/__tests__ and src/app/api/operator/__tests__ finds those two ids only in catalog.test.ts's catalog sweep and in two read-path suites that SEED agent_proposals rows directly). The single in-catalog-but-absent id a test does use, set_daily_cap, is not registered at all, so it is rejected by the earlier branch at render.ts:227-229 and continues before reaching 231. Recorded as P1 (uncovered change) rather than P0: the rule is also unreachable in production today — modelVisibleOperations (src/lib/agents/operator/catalog.ts:193-203) returns every CATALOG entry and ignores its tier parameter, so snapshot.allowedOperations always equals the catalog — which makes this a forward guard for Run B's tier-gated operations rather than a live hole in the no-unapproved-operation path. findings.reason: An uncovered behaviour-affecting production hunk (Direction B, Step 2). This is the branch that makes an exhausted account budget TERMINAL instead of burning the BullMQ retry ladder: isBudgetDecision(error) -> failTurnFenced with TURN_FAILURE_REASON.BUDGET_EXCEEDED. Neither budget_exceeded nor BUDGET_EXCEEDED nor isBudgetDecision appears in any test file in the repository, and no test on this lane constructs a CostLimitExceededError or a GlobalCostLimitExceededError. The sibling transient branch immediately below it IS covered ("worker releases its claim on a transient failure so the retry re-claims and completes"), and so is the exhausted reason in failed-hook.test.ts:107 — budget_exceeded is the one terminal reason with no case. The intake names it in both observability ("agent_turns.status and failure_reason distinguish failed reasons (... budget_exceeded)") and edge_cases ("Terminal failure (... budget exceeded ...)").
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Recorded without spending a mutation run: the absence of the token from every test file is direct evidence that no oracle exists, and the round budget was exhausted. Severity P1 rather than P0 because a miss is bounded — the cost RESERVATION precedes the model call, so a budget-exceeded error that fell through to the retry ladder would spend nothing extra and would end as failure_reason "exhausted" via the failed-hook instead of "budget_exceeded". The defect would therefore be an observability regression on a reason the intake promises to distinguish, not lost money or a stranded turn.

findings.title: agent_turn is missing from checkFailedOutboxByTopic's closed allowlist, so no health-alert finding can fire for a failed turn
findings.reason: A missing alert-path half: the branch adds an owner-impacting outbox topic and no emitting signal watches it. The allowlist binds exactly PUBLISH_RESPONSE, SEND_NOTIFICATION, GENERATE_RESPONSE, BUILD_SOLICITATION_BATCH, GENERATE_SOLICITATION_ASKS and SOLICITATION_VETO_NOTICE; QUEUE_NAMES.AGENT_TURN (src/lib/shared/queue-names.ts:68) is absent. A failed agent_turn row therefore raises no subsystem:health_alert finding, so rule 1 of docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md can never fire for this lane. Fix: add QUEUE_NAMES.AGENT_TURN to the allowlist, or state in the runbook why a failed turn is not owner-impacting.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The code comment directly above the allowlist names this exact defect class as a prior incident — "This is a CLOSED allowlist, so a new owner-impacting topic stays invisible until it is added here. generate_solicitation_asks shipped without it (#628 round 5), which silently voided that lane's dead-letter rationale: its terminal handler concedes the batch to 'an operator will see the failed row', and nothing was watching the row." The owner-impact test is met: a failed agent_turn means the owner's Operator message never receives a reply, and the branch's own design leans on the row being seen (docs/roadmap/2026-09-11-owner-operator/README.md:636 defers the stranded-turn case to Run B on exactly that basis). Verified independently of the subagent that surfaced it: I re-read checks.ts:105-124 and confirmed the six bound topics, and "rg -in agent_turn|owner.operator|worker_job docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md" returns zero matches.

findings.title: The job-failure-sink Sentry signal for queue agent_turn has no rule row in beta-launch-alerting.md
findings.reason: The other missing half: an emitted signal with no rule row. worker/index.ts registers agentTurnWorker into workersByQueue, and the existing loop attaches attachJobFailureSink to every entry, so BullMQ terminal exhaustion on this lane fires Sentry.captureException tagged {subsystem: "worker_job", queue: "agent_turn", topic}. That tag set matches no _If_ filter in the runbook's rule table and is not listed in the runbook's own register of signals that knowingly have no dedicated rule. Facet compared and contradicted: signal identity and filter (no rule selects this tag set) and destination action (no documented destination). Fix: add a rule row for subsystem:worker_job scoped to this queue, with a cadence, or extend the existing register to acknowledge it.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Scoped deliberately to the lane this branch adds rather than opened as a front against the sink, which is unchanged code: the finding is that the branch wires a NEW queue into an existing emitter and ships no rule for it. The runbook keeps an explicit list of signals that have no dedicated rule, which is what makes an unlisted, unrowed signal a reportable omission rather than an accepted posture.

findings.title: The orphaned-lease signal the intake names is a log line only — no Sentry event, no rule row
findings.reason: The intake's observability section states: "job_outbox rows for topic agent_turn: a stuck 'dispatched' row past the watchdog window is the signal a lease was orphaned." Both branches of runOutboxWatchdogRecovery — re-pending a stale dispatched row, and terminalising it to failed — only emit a structured log line, aggregated across every topic rather than broken out per topic, and neither captures to Sentry. Combined with P1-2, a worker crash that strands an agent_turn row in dispatched past the watchdog window produces zero Sentry event end to end: nothing from the watchdog, and nothing from checkFailedOutboxByTopic once the row lands failed. Facet contradicted: destination action — the contract names a signal that has no operator-actionable destination.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Reported against the contract the branch wrote rather than against OutboxPoller, which is unchanged: the claim that this row IS the orphaned-lease signal is new on this branch, and it is the claim that fails. Fixing P1-2 alone resolves the terminalised half of this; the re-pend half stays a log line, which is defensible if the runbook says so. Closing either the code or the contract sentence would settle it.

findings.title: A changed doc claim is false: the agent_turn lane does not emit logger.warn uniformly across the six terminal paths
findings.reason: The bullet, added by this branch inside the @@ -627,14 +627,37 @@ hunk, asserts that every terminal path in AgentTurnWorker — naming operator_disabled first — "resolves the turn and emits a logger.warn line", and concludes "That is uniform across the six paths, not a gap in one of them". At HEAD the operator_disabled path emits logger.log (worker/jobs/agent-turn/AgentTurnWorker.ts:324, "agent_turn flag-off skip"); the other five use logger.warn (AgentTurnWorker.ts:122, :171, :204, :229, :292). Fix: say five of the six paths warn and the flag-off skip logs at info, or change line 324 to warn.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Re-derived at HEAD, not taken from the subagent report: I read the bullet and the six call sites myself and confirmed the hunk membership with git diff. Recorded as P1 rather than P0 after weighing the "misleading FALSE claim" bar. The bullet's operative assertions are all true and independently verified here — there is no Sentry call anywhere in AgentTurnWorker.ts, and beta-launch-alerting.md carries no row for the lane — and the same sentence itself describes operator_disabled as "an orderly flag-off skip ... not an incident", which is consistent with logger.log being deliberate. A reader is therefore misled about one path's log LEVEL, not about whether the lane is alerted or about the single go-live decision the bullet defers. The concrete harm is bounded to whoever later implements that deferred decision with a level:warn filter and silently drops every operator_disabled turn. Recorded at P1 with this reasoning so the owner can escalate it to P0 if they weigh the uniformity assertion as load-bearing.

Recorded as P1 rather than P0 because the substantive safety claim — each site guards typeof-string, narrows and throws — is true at the real sites, and the enumeration's count and totals are correct; what is wrong is where to look, which is a stale reference of the same family as a stale line number.

findings.title: The branch adds a fifth private boundedErrorClass copy and picks the unhardened shape, while a hardened shared export already exists
findings.reason: Missed sibling case. Pattern searched: "function boundedErrorClass" across worker and src. Scope: the whole worker and src trees, no exclusions. Result: five definitions — the shared export at worker/jobs/solicitation-batch/failed-hook-shared.ts:36 (already imported by worker/jobs/solicitation-send/failed-hook.ts, worker/jobs/solicitation-batch/generate-failed-hook.ts and worker/jobs/solicitation-batch/failed-hook.ts) plus four private copies, the newest being this branch's. The shared one validates the class name against /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_$]{0,99}$/ and falls back to UnknownError, with a docblock giving the reason ("so a hostile or exotic error type cannot inject structure into the log line"); this branch's copy takes err.name unvalidated and slices it to 100 characters, then interpolates it into markOutboxFailed's reason string at failed-hook.ts:56-61, i.e. into a stored job_outbox error value and a log field. The same refactor commit that produced this HEAD (15bc4a4aa) deduplicated parseJsonbObject for exactly this shape; fallow's duplication gate does not reach a two-line helper. Fix: import boundedErrorClass from the shared module, or move it somewhere both hooks can share.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: P2, recorded and non-blocking, because there is no exploitable path today: the errors that reach this hook come from the LLM seam, Postgres and the cost guard, none of which sets .name from provider or owner text, and the value is a bound parameter rather than interpolated SQL. The finding is the divergence itself — the branch replicated the weaker of two existing siblings (worker/jobs/judge/failed-hook.ts:39) when a hardened shared export with a stated rationale was available.
